_comment: UI-2 lint extent controls. Consumed by src/__tests__/ui2LintExtent.test.ts.
These live in JSON, not in the test source, deliberately: eslint.config.js's colour selectors match ANY
string or template literal, not only style-object properties, so a known-bad fixture held as a source
string would make the guard test fail the very rule it asserts. Putting the test in an exempt directory
would also work and was rejected: an extent assertion must not depend on where it sits relative to the
exemptions of the config it is asserting. JSON is invisible to the **/*.{ts,tsx} files glob.

ignore.why: Token reference: values arrive as identifiers/member expressions, never as literals, so no selector applies. Note the token object must arrive by prop, not by import: a module outside src/components that does `import { tokens } from '../../theme/tokens'` fires the separate UI-3 import ban (verified), which would make the fixture noisy for the wrong reason.
ignore.source: export const Card = ({ t }: { t: { spaceMd: string; fg: string } }) => <div style={{ padding: t.spaceMd, color: t.fg }} />;

ignore.why: Unitless ratio. lineHeight is deliberately absent from DIM_CAMEL and DIM_KEBAB; a widening that added it would red-flag every legal ratio.
Flex factors and order are unitless structural numbers, deliberately outside DIM_CAMEL (comment at lines 18-19).
ignore.source: export const Card = () => <div style={{ flex: 1, flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 1, order: 2 }} />;

ignore.why: Integer zIndex is a stacking ordinal, not a dimension; deliberately outside DIM_CAMEL.

Percentages on gated keys. The numeric selector matches Literal.raw, which for a string includes its quotes and so cannot match ^\d+$, and the unit selector requires px or rem. Both structural, both deliberate.
ignore.source: export const Card = () => <div style={{ width: '100%', maxWidth: '50%' }} />;

ignore.why: Viewport units on gated keys pass the same way percentages do. Deliberate allowlist.
ignore.source: export const Card = () => <div style={{ height: '100vh', minHeight: '50vmin' }} />;

ignore.why: ch, fr and the auto keyword on gated keys. Deliberate allowlist.
ignore.source: export const Card = () => <div style={{ maxWidth: '60ch', width: 'auto', gridTemplateColumns: '1fr 2fr' }} />;

ignore.why: Literal zero, excluded explicitly by the (?!0$) lookahead in the numeric selectors. Zero carries no design decision.
ignore.source: export const Card = () => <div style={{ margin: 0, padding: 0 }} />;

ignore.why: KNOWN GAP (E-31): a computed key. esquery reads key.name of the computed Identifier ('key'), not the property it resolves to, so every key.name and key.value selector in the file misses. Unverified by a plant; measured here by driving ESLint against the config.
ignore.source:
const key = 'padding' as const;
export const Card = () => <div style={{ [key]: 24 }} />;

ignore.why: KNOWN GAP (E-31): one level of indirection through a module-local constant defeats every selector, and a local const is not a token. This is the shape a raw-value drift takes once anyone hits the rule once. Structurally indistinguishable from a legitimate token reference to a syntactic linter, which is why closing it needs a different mechanism, not a wider selector. Unverified by a plant; measured here by driving ESLint against the config.
ignore.source:
const PAD = 24;
export const Card = () => <div style={{ padding: PAD }} />;
